name: Tharsis Region
description: Vast volcanic plateau elevated up to 10 km above surrounding lowlands, hosting the colossal Tharsis Montes and Olympus Mons.
geology: Extensive Hesperian-to-Amazonian basaltic lava flows underlain by a massive mantle plume swell.

name: Arabia Terra
description: Heavily cratered, ancient Noachian highland terrain exhibiting cyclic layered deposits and remnants of supervolcano calderas.
geology: Noachian crust with explosive volcanism and ancient friable layered sulfate deposits.

name: Terra Cimmeria
description: Densely cratered southern highlands preserving the strongest magnetic crustal stripes, indicating an ancient Martian core dynamo.
geology: Ancient Noachian basement with remanent crustal magnetization and valley network incisions.

name: Terra Sirenum
description: Rugged southern upland characterized by recurring slope lineae (RSL), chloride mineral salt flats, and inverted river channels.
geology: Noachian-to-Hesperian impact breccia and chloride salt playa deposits.

name: Xanthe Terra
description: Highland border zone carved by dramatic sinuous valleys and outflow channels draining toward Chryse Planitia.
geology: Sapping valley systems, incised river gorges, and fractured bedrock.

name: Noachis Terra
description: The type locality for the Noachian geological epoch (~4.1-3.7 Ga); ancient heavily cratered terrain situated between Argyre and Hellas basins.
geology: Primitive planetary crust heavily degraded by the Late Heavy Bombardment.

name: Elysium Region
description: The second largest volcanic center on Mars, characterized by Elysium Mons, Hecates Tholus, Albor Tholus, and young Cerberus Fossae fissures.
geology: Late Hesperian to Amazonian shield volcanism and catastrophic flood lavas.

name: Amazonis Planitia
description: One of the smoothest and least cratered plains on Mars, defining the youngest Martian epoch (the Amazonian).
geology: Extremely young, pristine basaltic flood lavas thinly blanketed by bright atmospheric dust.

name: Arcadia Planitia
description: Northern smooth plain holding vast, shallow subsurface water ice sheets accessible within 1-2 meters of the surface.
geology: Glacio-lacustrine and volcanic plains with periglacial polygon patterned ground.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: Massive circular northern basin holding an estimated volume of water ice equivalent to Lake Superior. Landing site of Viking 2 and Zhurong.
geology: Sedimentary infill over buried impact basin with scallops and polygon ice wedges.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: Ancient Noachian impact basin at the transition between southern highlands and northern lowlands. Jezero Crater sits on its western rim.
geology: Modified impact basin filled with Hesperian sedimentary and volcanic material.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: The deepest planetary impact basin on Mars and in the solar system, plunging to -7,152 meters. Surface pressure is ~1,155 Pa, permitting pure water to theoretically exist as liquid briefly.
geology: Noachian basin floor modified by glaciers, fluvial inflows (Dao, Harmakhis, Niger), and eolian dunes.

name: Chryse Planitia
description: The 'Plain of Gold' — circular lowland plain where multiple colossal flood channels (Ares, Tiu, Simud, Kasei) discharged catastrophic floodwaters.
geology: Fluvial flood sedimentary deposits and volcanic wrinkle ridges. Viking 1 and Pathfinder landed here.

name: Margaritifer Terra
description: Heavily fractured region displaying the greatest concentration of chaotic terrain (Aram Chaos, Hydraotes Chaos) and channel origins.
geology: Catastrophic collapse of groundwater aquifers generating regional chaos blocks.

name: Meridiani Planum
description: The Martian prime meridian datum plain, famous for grey crystalline hematite spherules ('blueberries') explored by NASA's Opportunity rover.
geology: Layered sulfate-rich sandstones formed in ancient acidic, shallow groundwater lake environments.

name: Vastitas Borealis
description: The vast northern circumpolar waste surrounding Planum Boreum. NASA Phoenix lander touched down here in 2008 and scraped subsurface water ice.
geology: Periglacial terrain, polygon grounds, pattern soils, and buried pure water ice slabs.

name: Terra Sabaea
description: Highland plateau exhibiting lobate debris aprons (glacier-like viscous ice-rock flows) and pristine layered craters.
geology: Noachian crust with debris-covered glaciers and clay mineral deposits.

name: Tempe Terra
description: Extensively faulted highland plateau situated northeast of Tharsis Montes, dissected by complex graben systems.
geology: Tectonic extension grabens, volcanic fissure vents, and ancient cratered terrain.
